newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN body wants death penalty scrapped, US against.
newsitem.headline: UN body wants death penalty scrapped, US against.

text.p: The United States was the only Western nation on Thursday to vote against a U.N. human rights commission resolution urging countries to consider abolishing capital punishment.
The resolution, sponsored by Italy but not legally binding, passed in Geneva with a simple majority of 27 in favour, 11 against and 14 abstentions.

Washington and Beijing, which have repeatedly clashed at the forum over U.S. charges of Chinese rights violations, both voted against the resolution, as did Algeria, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Egypt, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Pakistan and South Korea.
Last year, the respected International Commission of Jurists (ICJ) accused the United States of carrying out death sentences that were arbitrary and racially discriminatory against blacks.

It said 40 percent of the people executed in the United States between 1973 and 1995 were black. It noted that blacks also made up 44 percent of the U.S. prison population although Americans of African origin accounted for six percent of the U.S. population.
The resolution calls on all countries that have not yet abolished the death penalty to restrict the number of sentences, to avoid using it too often and to consider suspending future executions.

Countries that voted for the resolution included the former Soviet republics of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus as well as South Africa, Angola, Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Mexico, Mozambique, Nepal and Nicaragua.
Britain was the only European Union member state to abstain, along with countries such as Zaire, Cuba, Uganda, El Salvador, Ethiopia, Pakistan and India.
